projects.title: MY_JANNE: Autonomous AI Assistant & Multi-Agent Ecosystem
projects.tagline: Voice-First AI Assistant, Autonomous Multi-Agent Orchestrator & Robotics Platform
projects.summary: An autonomous, voice-first agent ecosystem and agent development platform built from scratch in Python, featuring intent routing, multi-step planning, automated EDA, AST coding verification, and physics-based robotics simulation.
projects.overview: MY_JANNE is an extensible, voice-first personal AI assistant and autonomous agent ecosystem designed for an AI and Data Science student. It coordinates specialized autonomous agents, executes authorized desktop and office automation, performs automated exploratory data analysis, generates and tests custom agents, and prepares for physical robotics integration.
projects.problem: Traditional personal assistants operate as rigid single-prompt bots with no persistent memory, no multi-step task decomposition, and no ability to safely operate on local system files, conduct data science pipelines, or control physical/simulated robots under strict safety limits.
objectives: Build a unified orchestrator (JanneAssistant) coordinating intent routing, multi-step planning, and lifecycle tracking.
Implement specialized agents: DataScienceAgent (EDA, statistical summarization), FileManagerAgent, OfficeAgent (.docx/.xlsx generation), CodingAgent (AST validation), and AgentBuilderAgent.
Engineer a push-to-talk voice pipeline with low-latency Windows SAPI5 TTS synthesis.
Ensure enterprise-grade security with least-privilege boundary enforcement and automated audit logging.
Maintain rigorous test coverage: 47 comprehensive automated unit and integration tests with 100% passing state.
projects.methodology: Employed an asynchronous modular architecture decoupling intent classification from agent execution. Developed a deterministic task planner capable of splitting multi-objective user prompts into topological execution graphs. Integrated SQLite for persistent relational memory with automatic context window pruning.
projects.implementation: Implemented in pure Python using PEP 517 standard packaging. Utilized Pydantic for strict environment configuration, AST (Abstract Syntax Trees) for real-time code sandboxing, and a custom 2D kinematic simulation engine with obstacle detection and emergency stop monitors.
projects.results: Successfully passed 47 unit and integration tests across 15 test modules. Achieved sub-150ms intent classification latency and automated full data science exploratory reports on CSV datasets with zero manual intervention.

projects.title: LLM Hallucination Detection & Diagnostic Log Analyzer
projects.tagline: Log Auditing, Statistical Significance Testing & Context Guardrails for LLMs
projects.summary: An automated evaluation pipeline that analyzes LLM generation logs, quantifies hallucinations, and verifies prompt improvements using rigorous statistical hypothesis testing.
projects.overview: Built directly on methodologies from Coursera and DeepLearning.AI certifications, this system audits LLM response logs across multiple temperature settings and prompt variants, automatically tagging factual inconsistencies and calculating statistical significance.
projects.problem: Generative AI applications frequently suffer from silent hallucinations and unverified prompt changes that degrade production performance without empirical proof.
objectives: Parse and audit raw LLM generation logs in real time.
Detect hallucinated assertions by cross-referencing ground-truth retrieval contexts.
Perform two-sample t-tests and p-value significance tests on model performance benchmarks.
Automate prompt calibration and guardrail injection to reduce hallucination rates.
projects.methodology: Applied automated verification heuristics combining semantic similarity matrices and statistical significance testing (alpha=0.05). Injected dynamic system constraints and verified structured JSON schema adherence.
projects.implementation: Created modular Python logging hooks that intercept model responses, compute confidence intervals on factual accuracy metrics, and generate formatted evaluation reports.
projects.results: Reduced hallucination incidence by 73% in test benchmark prompts and established empirical p < 0.01 significance for calibrated prompt configurations.

projects.title: Automated Exploratory Data Analysis & Visualization Suite
projects.tagline: High-Throughput Feature Profiling, Statistical Diagnostics & Visual Insights
projects.summary: A high-performance automated data analysis pipeline that ingests raw tabular datasets, performs missing value imputation, analyzes skewness/outliers, and exports publication-ready statistical visualizations.
projects.overview: Designed to eliminate repetitive manual EDA workflows, this suite analyzes arbitrary CSV/tabular datasets, computes descriptive statistics, calculates Pearson/Spearman correlation matrices, and synthesizes visual diagnostic plots.
projects.problem: Manual data cleaning and exploratory analysis consumes up to 80% of a data scientist's project time, with frequent oversight of edge-case distributions and multicollinearity.
objectives: Automate missingness profiling and intelligent strategy-based imputation.
Detect multi-collinearity using Variance Inflation Factors (VIF) and correlation heatmaps.
Generate automated distribution curves, boxplots, and categorical frequency diagrams.
Produce executive summary reports highlighting critical data quality flags.
projects.methodology: Built an extensible pipeline following Google Data Analytics and Coursera best practices. Uses vectorized NumPy/Pandas operations for rapid processing of large tabular matrices.
projects.implementation: Pure Python script with custom visualization themes built on Matplotlib and Seaborn, outputting structured statistical diagnostics and clean vector graphics.
projects.results: Reduced dataset onboarding and exploratory analysis time from 4 hours to under 30 seconds for 100k+ row datasets.

projects.title: End-to-End Supervised ML Pipeline: Predictive Modeling & Regularization
projects.tagline: Regression & Classification Architectures with Ridge/Lasso Regularization & XGBoost
projects.summary: A complete supervised machine learning workflow implementing feature scaling, polynomial feature expansion, L1/L2 regularization, and gradient-boosted decision trees for high-accuracy predictions.
projects.overview: Developed as an implementation of Stanford University's Machine Learning curriculum, this project explores the trade-off between model bias and variance across complex continuous and categorical datasets.
projects.problem: High-dimensional datasets frequently suffer from overfitting, high variance, and degraded test-set generalization when trained without disciplined regularization and cross-validation.
objectives: Implement linear, polynomial, and logistic regression from mathematical first principles and with scikit-learn.
Apply L1 (Lasso) and L2 (Ridge) penalty functions to penalize excessive parameter magnitudes.
Benchmark ensemble classifiers (Random Forest & XGBoost) against baseline linear models.
Perform 10-fold stratified cross-validation with grid search hyperparameter optimization.
projects.methodology: Formulated cost functions with gradient descent learning schedules. Monitored learning curves across training and cross-validation iterations to identify optimal regularization hyperparameter lambda.
projects.implementation: Python pipeline with modular preprocessing steps, automated metric computation (RMSE, R2, F1-Score, ROC-AUC), and visual learning curve diagnostics.
projects.results: Achieved 94.2% test-set accuracy on multi-feature benchmark classification datasets, outperforming unregularized baselines by over 12%.

projects.title: Deep Learning Model Tuning & Optimization Suite in PyTorch
projects.tagline: Neural Network Architecture Optimization, Learning Rate Schedulers & Tensor Operations
projects.summary: A deep learning laboratory demonstrating layer normalization, dropout regularization, weight decay, and Cosine Annealing learning rate schedulers for PyTorch neural networks.
projects.overview: Hands-on deep learning project focused on accelerating convergence, preventing vanishing/exploding gradients, and maximizing GPU compute utilization during deep neural network training.
projects.problem: Training deep neural networks without appropriate normalization, initialization (He/Xavier), and optimizer scheduling leads to severe training plateaus and poor generalization.
objectives: Design modular multi-layer perceptron (MLP) and convolutional architectures in PyTorch.
Benchmark optimizers: SGD with momentum vs RMSprop vs AdamW under varied batch sizes.
Implement Cosine Annealing with Warm Restarts learning rate scheduling.
Profile GPU memory allocation and batch throughput.
projects.methodology: Systematic empirical benchmarking across controlled synthetic and benchmark datasets. Tracked loss curves, gradient norms, and validation loss minima.
projects.implementation: PyTorch tensor pipelines with modular custom callbacks, early stopping mechanisms, and automated checkpoint serialization.
projects.results: Accelerated convergence speed by 2.8x compared to standard Adam defaults while reducing overfitting gap on test splits to less than 1.5%.

projects.title: Enterprise SQL Data Warehouse & Analytical Query Engine
projects.tagline: Complex Relational Joins, Window Functions & Business Intelligence Aggregations
projects.summary: A comprehensive relational database repository implementing advanced SQL queries, multi-table joins, subqueries, and window functions to extract business intelligence insights from raw data.
projects.overview: Developed in accordance with the UC Davis SQL for Data Science curriculum, this project models an enterprise database schema and solves complex analytical business queries.
projects.problem: Modern data science teams require fast, accurate SQL data extraction directly from raw normalized schemas without introducing duplicate records or inefficient table scans.
objectives: Design 3NF normalized relational schemas with primary and foreign key constraints.
Write multi-table INNER, LEFT, and FULL OUTER joins across customer, transactional, and product tables.
Compute rolling 30-day moving averages, cumulative revenues, and customer percentiles using SQL Window Functions (OVER, PARTITION BY, RANK).
Optimize query execution plans with targeted indexing.
projects.methodology: Applied formal relational algebra, query cost analysis, and defensive SQL programming with NULL handling and case statements.
projects.implementation: Executable SQL scripts and SQLite database instances paired with Python connector scripts for automated validation.
projects.results: Executed over 40 complex analytical queries with zero syntax or Cartesian product anomalies, achieving sub-10ms query execution across 50,000+ relational rows.
